node.title: Re: Print hash keys and lookup the keys for values in another filr
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [Magnolia25],

Note that your code contains some errors that prevent it from compiling. I'm going to assume you copied the code you showed out of a larger program and that you've actually got use warnings; use strict; and the missing variable declarations. In the future, please try to provide code that compiles ([id://1177642|SSCCE]).

First, in last if !line;, you're missing the $ sigil from $line.

Second, note how you've got a comma in (split(/;/, $line)),[1,0]. This is creating several values: the return values of [doc://split], plus the anonymous array [1,0]. What you probably meant is (split...)[1,0], which returns a list consisting of the second return value of [doc://split] followed by the first return value of the [doc://split].

If you fix these issues, you've still got a conceptual problem. The way I understand it, you're trying to store a hash with multiple values per key. One way to do this is with a "hash of arrays" or "hash of hashes", which are described with lots of example code in [doc://perldsc].

Because this sounds very much like a homework assignment, I'm reluctant to do too much of your work for you :-) However, if you look at [doc://perlreftut] and [doc://perldsc], I hope it will become more clear how you can accomplish your tasks:

  1. Read the file line-by-line, as you already are.
  2. [doc://split] the line into its columns*.
  3. Store the values in your hash of hashes, such as $hash{$col[1]}{$col[0]}=1;, or into a hash of arrays via push @{ $hash{$col[1]} }, $col[0]; (see [doc://push]).

* For parsing files like this, it really would be best to use a module like [mod://Text::CSV].

Your "Step 2" sounds very much like "Step 1", except with different columns. If you also need to filter the "Step 2" input file, I would suggest that you store the first column from your "Step 1" input file in a hash, and when you're parsing your "Step 2" input file, seeing if that value [doc://exists] in the hash you created.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
